title: Your Brain Gets a Privacy Policy
script: It is 2038. Your insurance app asks for brain data. Sharing is optional. So is the discount beside the button. At work, a second app offers focus analytics. It says the team will only see averages. You open the policy. The message you intended to send is only one part of the data being collected. You can refuse. But refusing now has a cost attached to it. The interface made communication easier. Would you trade neural privacy for a discount?
timingStatus: Estimated silent editorial timings. Refit scenes and caption timestamps to the unchanged voice-over when supplied.
concept: Insurance discounts and focus analytics make neural-data consent complicated.
whyNow: A present capability creates a plausible human decision; this is a scenario, not a forecast.
viewerGoal: Consider the human consequence and choose a boundary.
hooks: It is 2038. Your insurance app asks for brain data.
The discount asks for something more personal than money.
Sharing is optional. Refusing has a cost.
strongestHook: It is 2038. Your insurance app asks for brain data.
directorBrief: Direct this as a human story about Insurance discounts and focus analytics make neural-data consent complicated. Emotional movement: convenience → consent. Open with a recognisable person or object, introduce one consequence, then leave the final choice unresolved. Fictional dates and interfaces are scenario details. Facts must be separately sourced; use a small persistent POSSIBLE FUTURE label, never a news-like breaking banner.
effort: 60–120 minutes asset production and edit; no audio included.
protocol: Produce original story assets, review factual grounding, verify every future claim is conditional or explicitly fictional, then inspect continuity and safe zones. No real-world experiment outcome is claimed.
evidenceRequirements: Commercial neural-data offers are fiction; verify current medical/research context.
